chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara and Ma'mar ibn Yahya and Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

In the prayer upon the deceased, there is no specific recitation, nor a prescribed supplication; you may supplicate with whatever comes to your mind. The deceased have the most right that the believer supplicates for them, and that he begins with sending blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ عَلَى الْمَيِّتِ: Funeral prayer / Prayer upon the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed method for recitation and supplication during the funeral prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that Salat al-Mayyit is a flexible act of supplication rather than a rigid ritual with fixed recitations, allowing the believer to invoke whatever they wish for the deceased. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the merit of the deceased being directly linked to the sincerity of the living, while also establishing the protocol of prioritizing blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a sign of respect and connection to the Ahl al-Bayt. This ruling underscores the practical accessibility of funeral prayers, removing barriers for laypeople while maintaining spiritual depth through personal du'a.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim and Zurara and Ma’mar Bin Yahya and Ismail Al Ju’fy, 
from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘In the Salaat upon the deceased there is neither a recitation (of a Chapter of the Holy Quran), nor any Prescribed supplication. You can supplicate with whatever comes to you, and it is a right of the deceased that the Believer should supplicate for him, and that he should begin with the sending of Blessings upon Rasool-Allahsaww’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ’Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah from and Mu’ammar ibn Yahya and ’Isma‘il al-Ju’fiy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

There is no particularly prescribed prayer to say in Salah (prayer) for a deceased. You can pray whatever prayer you like; and the most deserving is the believing person who has just died and that such prayer begins with prayer for the Messenger of Allah by saying, ‘O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’”
